data.narrative:
SkySafe, a Series B defense and security technology company that has raised $50M+, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 10 peers—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies in the same sector and stage. The private peer set includes Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Castelion, and Defense Unicorns.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $50M total raised as a proxy base, applying a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B progression, yielding $95M. The peer-median method draws from seven same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $300M to $3.0B; the median across this set is $1.0B. This wider dispersion reflects heterogeneity in capital efficiency and market positioning within the defense-tech space at Series B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $81M to $1.1B, with a median of $548M. The wide spread reflects tension between capital-deployed methodology (suggesting $95M) and peer-market valuation levels (suggesting $1.0B), indicating material uncertainty around SkySafe's relative traction, defensibility, and go-to-market momentum versus established cohort peers. Resolution of this gap hinges on revenue growth trajectory, customer concentration, and product differentiation relative to the identified comparable set.
